patient.name: Marcia Campbell
patient.complaint: Bulging veins in the right leg with aching, heaviness and itchy ankles
background: Hairdresser in Croydon, on her feet all day
Right calf DVT after her second baby

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' or 'most likely finding' with tortuous medial leg veins, aching by evening, skin changes at the ankle, or a groin lump with a cough impulse.

points: Marcia, 49, stands all day cutting hair.
Her right leg **aches and feels heavy by evening**.
Ankles swell by the end of the day.
Bulging blue veins have grown worse since her pregnancies.

steps.lead: Marcia's bulging veins are superficial veins stretched by **incompetent valves**, most often in the great saphenous system.
Marcia has **obesity** (the key risk factor), three pregnancies, a standing job and a previous DVT.

visual.title: Marcia's right ankle through a work day
visual.caption: Swelling and aching **build through the day** standing and ease overnight with the legs up.

points: Standing: tortuous veins along the **medial calf and thigh**.

steps.lead: Marcia's veins follow the **long saphenous** course, and her normal ABPI supports a venous rather than arterial problem.

steps.title: The great (long) saphenous vein
nodes: In front of the medial malleolus
Saphenofemoral junction into the femoral vein
steps.caption: The **small saphenous** drains the posterolateral leg into the popliteal vein.

steps.q: Marcia also has a soft bluish groin lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle that vanishes lying down. What is it?
steps.r: A **saphena varix** at the saphenofemoral junction: bluish, disappears lying down, positive **cough impulse**. An aneurysm is pulsatile.

steps.lead: Marcia's groin lump is a **saphena varix**, often mistaken for a femoral hernia: it has a cough impulse and empties when she lies down.
Marcia's ankle staining is **haemosiderin**; hard tight skin, eczema or an ulcer would follow. Sudden painful redness would mean thrombophlebitis or DVT.

steps.title: Painful leg in someone with varicose veins
head: Feature
Superficial thrombophlebitis
DVT
Cellulitis

steps.lead: Marcia has **pain** and skin changes, so she meets the criteria for vascular referral. Cosmetic concern alone would not.

investigation.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?': duplex venous ultrasound. ABPI appears before any compression treatment.

steps.q: Which test confirms Marcia's valve incompetence?
steps.r: **Duplex venous ultrasound** shows reflux and valve incompetence. ABPI checks the arteries; tourniquet tests are bedside and unreliable.

steps.lead: Marcia's **duplex ultrasound** maps exactly which valves leak and confirms the saphenofemoral junction is incompetent.

visual.title: Reflux time in Marcia's great saphenous vein
visual.label: Marcia 2.4 s
visual.caption: Backward flow lasting over **0.5 seconds** after calf squeeze means the valves are incompetent.

steps.title: Marcia's vascular clinic results
steps.text: Normal ABPI: compression would be safe. Deep veins patent, so ablation is suitable.
Duplex also checks the **deep veins** are patent. Ablating superficial veins in someone with deep vein occlusion removes their main drainage.
**Duplex** confirms varicose veins; **ABPI** is the safety check before compression. Know which test answers which question.

management.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate management?': conservative measures, then endothermal ablation first-line, foam sclerotherapy second, surgery third; compression never if ABPI below 0.8.

steps.lead: Marcia is advised to **elevate her legs**, lose weight and exercise. Compression is for symptom relief only if intervention is unsuitable, and never if ABPI is below 0.8.

visual.title: ABPI before compression
visual.label: Marcia 1.05
visual.caption: Marcia's ABPI is **above 0.8**, so stockings would be safe if needed.

steps.q: Marcia has symptomatic great saphenous reflux. What is first-line interventional treatment?
steps.r: **Endothermal ablation** (EVLA or radiofrequency) first; foam sclerotherapy second; surgery third.

steps.lead: Marcia is booked for **endothermal ablation**. If unsuitable, she would have **ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy**.
If both failed or were unsuitable, Marcia would have **surgical ligation and stripping**.

steps.title: Varicose vein ladder
nodes: Refer if bleeding, pain, thrombophlebitis, ulcer, skin change
steps.caption: Compression only if intervention is unsuitable, and only with ABPI ≥0.8.

steps.lead: Marcia's ankle staining is treated with **emollients** and compression, plus vascular review. If she got thrombophlebitis: **NSAIDs**, adding **LMWH** near the SFJ.

steps.text: Thrombophlebitis **within 3 cm of the saphenofemoral junction** can extend into the femoral vein. Add LMWH and scan; do not just give an NSAID.

science.exam: Expect applied questions: why incompetent valves raise venous pressure, why the skin turns brown, how ablation works and why ABPI must be checked before compression.

steps.lead: Marcia's leaky valves let blood fall **back down** the leg under gravity, raising pressure in her superficial veins.

steps.title: From leaky valve to ulcer
nodes: Capillary damage, red cells leak out

steps.lead: Red cells leak from Marcia's damaged capillaries; their **haemosiderin** stains her ankle brown, and fibrosis will harden it (**lipodermatosclerosis**).

steps.q: How does endothermal ablation fix Marcia's symptoms?
o: Heat makes the vein fibrose and close
steps.r: Heat causes **fibrosis and occlusion** of the incompetent vein, so blood returns through the competent **deep** veins.

steps.lead: The laser fibre heats Marcia's great saphenous vein so it **scars shut**; blood reroutes through her healthy deep veins.
Marcia's ABPI was checked first because squeezing a leg with poor **arterial** inflow can make it ischaemic.

mcq.r: **Incompetent valves** cause reflux and venous hypertension.

mcq.q: Which vein is most commonly affected?
What is the key risk factor for varicose veins in the notes?
Which sign is positive with a saphena varix?
mcq.r: A saphena varix has a positive **cough impulse** and empties lying down.

mcq.q: Which is a criterion for vascular referral?
mcq.r: Bleeding, pain, **thrombophlebitis**, ulceration or severe impact on quality of life.
**Duplex venous ultrasound** shows reflux and valve incompetence.

mcq.q: What is the first-line interventional treatment?
Below which ABPI are compression stockings contraindicated?
mcq.r: ABPI **<0.8** suggests arterial disease; compression could cause ischaemia.

mcq.q: What causes the brown pigmentation of chronic venous insufficiency?
mcq.r: **Haemosiderin** from red cells leaking out of damaged capillaries.

prompts.q: What are varicose veins and what causes them?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: valve, reflux, pressure, vein.

prompts.q: Who gets varicose veins? Name the risk factors.
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: the stem gives the job and the BMI.

points.why: The key risk factor in the notes.
Raised pelvic venous pressure and hormones.

prompts.q: How do varicose veins present, and where do the saphenous veins run?

points.p: Visible dilated tortuous veins along the medial calf (long saphenous)
Aching, heavy legs and swelling worse at the end of the day
Long saphenous: dorsum of big toe, front of medial malleolus, medial thigh, femoral vein
Short saphenous drains the posterolateral lower leg

prompts.q: What are the complications of varicose veins, and which one is an emergency?

points.why: Brown staining at the gaiter area.

points.p: Sudden painful swelling/redness: superficial thrombophlebitis or DVT

prompts.q: What is a saphena varix and how do you recognise it?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: groin lump with a cough impulse.

points.p: Inferior and lateral to the pubic tubercle
points.why: Same place as a femoral hernia.

points.p: Bluish tinge, disappears when lying down

points.why: Can also have a fluid thrill on tapping the vein.

prompts.q: When should varicose veins be referred to vascular surgery?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: list them; cosmetic alone is the distractor.

points.why: Can be brisk from a thin-walled vein.
Tender red cord along a varicose vein.

points.p: Severe impact on quality of life; not cosmetic alone
points.why: Cosmetic concern alone does not qualify.

prompts.q: What is the gold-standard investigation and what does it show?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: the scan for veins.

points.p: Shows venous reflux and valve incompetence
ABPI before compression to exclude arterial disease

prompts.q: Describe the treatment ladder for varicose veins.
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: conservative, then ablation, foam, surgery.

points.p: Conservative: leg elevation, weight loss, exercise
Compression stockings only if intervention unsuitable; not if ABPI <0.8
Second-line: ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (sodium tetradecyl sulfate)

prompts.q: How are the complications of varicose veins managed?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: skin care and clot care.

points.p: Skin changes: emollients and graduated compression
Add LMWH if extensive or near the saphenofemoral junction
points.why: Risk of extending into the deep system.

points.p: Refer skin changes to vascular surgery

prompts.q: Why do incompetent valves cause skin changes, and how does ablation work?
prompts.tip: Exam thinking: pressure, leak, stain, scar.

points.p: Valves normally ensure one-way flow towards the heart
Incompetent: reflux under gravity raises venous pressure
Capillary damage and RBC extravasation deposit haemosiderin
Ablation: heat causes fibrosis and occlusion; flow redirects to deep veins
points.why: The vein is closed, not repaired.

points.p: ABPI first: compression worsens ischaemia in arterial disease

glossary.varicose veins: Dilated, twisted superficial veins caused by leaky valves.
glossary.incompetent valve: A vein valve that no longer closes properly, letting blood flow backwards.
glossary.venous reflux: Backward flow of blood in a vein because the valves leak.
glossary.venous hypertension: Raised pressure in the leg veins from reflux or obstruction.
glossary.chronic venous insufficiency: Long-term failure of leg veins to return blood, causing swelling and skin changes.
glossary.great saphenous vein: The long superficial vein running up the inner leg into the femoral vein.
glossary.long saphenous vein: Another name for the great saphenous vein.
glossary.short saphenous vein: Superficial vein of the back of the calf that drains into the popliteal vein.
glossary.small saphenous vein: Another name for the short saphenous vein.
glossary.saphenofemoral junction: Where the great saphenous vein joins the femoral vein in the groin.
glossary.SFJ: Saphenofemoral junction: where the great saphenous vein meets the femoral vein.
glossary.saphena varix: A swelling of the great saphenous vein at the groin with a cough impulse.
glossary.cough impulse: A palpable bulge in a groin lump when the patient coughs.
glossary.pubic tubercle: A small bony bump on the pubic bone, a key groin landmark.
glossary.medial malleolus: The bony bump on the inner ankle.
glossary.lipodermatosclerosis: Hard, tight, fibrosed skin and fat of the lower leg from chronic venous disease.
glossary.haemosiderin: Iron pigment from broken-down red cells that stains skin brown.
glossary.venous eczema: Itchy, scaly inflamed skin of the lower leg from venous hypertension.
glossary.venous ulcer: Shallow irregular ulcer above the medial malleolus from chronic venous hypertension.
glossary.superficial thrombophlebitis: Clot and inflammation in a superficial vein: a hard, tender, red cord.
glossary.DVT: Deep vein thrombosis: a clot in a deep vein of the leg or pelvis.
glossary.duplex ultrasound: Ultrasound combining images and Doppler flow to show reflux and clots.
glossary.ABPI: Ankle-brachial pressure index: ankle systolic divided by arm systolic pressure.
glossary.compression stockings: Graduated elastic stockings that squeeze the leg to help venous return.
glossary.endothermal ablation: Closing a leaky vein from inside using heat from a laser or radiofrequency.
glossary.EVLA: Endovenous laser ablation: heat from a laser fibre closes the vein.
glossary.radiofrequency ablation: Closing a vein from inside using radiofrequency heat.
glossary.foam sclerotherapy: Injecting a foam that irritates and scars a vein shut, guided by ultrasound.
glossary.sodium tetradecyl sulfate: A sclerosant drug used to make foam for sclerotherapy.
glossary.ligation and stripping: Surgery tying off the vein at the junction and pulling it out.
glossary.LMWH: Low molecular weight heparin, an injected anticoagulant such as enoxaparin.
glossary.NSAIDs: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen.
glossary.emollient: A moisturiser that softens and protects dry skin.
glossary.extravasation: Leakage of blood cells or fluid out of vessels into tissue.
glossary.Trendelenburg test: Bedside tourniquet test of where venous reflux occurs, now replaced by duplex.

technique.stem: A 55 year old man who works as a chef has aching in his left leg at the end of each day. On standing, there are tortuous dilated veins over the back and outer side of his left calf, running up to the back of the knee. The inner thigh and calf are normal. Foot pulses are present.
technique.q: Which vein is most likely to be incompetent?

steps.x: Which vein? Use the distribution of the varicosities.

clues: back and outer side of his left calf
up to the back of the knee
inner thigh and calf are normal
steps.x: Posterolateral calf, draining to the popliteal fossa.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: A deep vein; not visible as varicosities.
Runs up the medial leg, which is normal here.
Deep vein receiving the small saphenous.

steps.x: **E.** Medial = great saphenous; posterolateral = small saphenous.

technique.stem: A 46 year old woman who is a nurse has bulging veins along her right medial calf and thigh with aching and ankle swelling by the evening. She wants treatment. Foot pulses are palpable. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 124/76 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?

clues: bulging veins along her right medial calf and thigh
aching and ankle swelling by the evening

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: A safety check of the arteries, not diagnostic.

technique.stem: A 58 year old woman has symptomatic varicose veins with great saphenous reflux on duplex ultrasound. The vein is too tortuous for a catheter to pass, so endothermal ablation is not technically possible. Her ABPI is 1.0. Her pulse rate is 70 bpm and BP 130/80 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate treatment?

steps.x: Treatment when first-line intervention is unsuitable.

clues: endothermal ablation is not technically possible

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Only if all intervention is unsuitable.
Conservative measures alone do not treat reflux.

technique.stem: A 51 year old man has endovenous laser ablation of his great saphenous vein for symptomatic reflux. Six weeks later his aching has gone. He asks how the treatment worked.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
o: Heat-induced fibrosis and occlusion of the vein

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Heat causes **fibrosis and occlusion**; flow goes through deep veins.

elim: There is no clot to dissolve.

steps.x: **B.** The vein is closed, not fixed.

practice.stem: A 52 year old woman who works in a supermarket has had aching, heavy legs for 2 years, worse by the evening. On standing, there are dilated tortuous veins along the medial aspect of her left calf and thigh. Foot pulses are present. Her pulse rate is 76 bpm and BP 128/78 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Dilated tortuous medial leg veins with evening aching in an obese woman who stands at work are great saphenous varicose veins. Normal ABPI excludes PAD.

steps.x: A diagnosis question about leg symptoms and visible veins.

clues: dilated tortuous veins along the medial aspect
steps.x: Standing job, gravity-dependent aching, great saphenous distribution.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: DVT is acute calf swelling and pain, not 2 years.
Lymphoedema is non-pitting swelling without visible veins.
ABPI is normal and pulses present.
Thrombophlebitis is an acute tender red cord.

practice.stem: A 60 year old man with long-standing varicose veins of the right leg has a soft lump in his right groin, below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. It has a bluish tinge when he stands and disappears when he lies down. His pulse rate is 70 bpm and BP 134/82 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination of the lump?
practice.e: This is a saphena varix at the saphenofemoral junction, which has a positive cough impulse. Expansile pulsation would suggest a femoral aneurysm.

steps.x: A finding question: name the lump first.

clues: below and lateral to the pubic tubercle

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: A hydrocele or cyst, not a vein.

steps.x: **D.** Saphena varix = cough impulse, empties lying down.

practice.stem: A 47 year old woman has visible tortuous veins running from the front of her left medial malleolus up the inner calf and inner thigh to the groin. She has three children and a BMI of 31 kg/m². Her pulse rate is 74 bpm and BP 122/76 mmHg.
practice.q: Which vein system is most likely to be affected?
practice.e: The great (long) saphenous vein runs in front of the medial malleolus, up the medial calf and thigh to the saphenofemoral junction.

clues: front of her left medial malleolus
inner calf and inner thigh to the groin

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: A deep vein behind the knee.

steps.x: **B.** Medial leg to groin = great saphenous.

practice.stem: A 66 year old woman with varicose veins for 20 years has itchy, brown discoloured skin above both medial malleoli. The skin of the lower third of her legs is hard, tight and woody, giving an 'inverted champagne bottle' shape. Foot pulses are present.
practice.q: Which skin complication is most likely?
practice.e: Hard, tight, fibrosed skin with haemosiderin pigmentation in chronic venous disease is lipodermatosclerosis.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Acute, hot and red, not chronic woody skin.
Graves' disease: raised waxy shin plaques.

practice.stem: A 54 year old man with varicose veins has 2 days of pain and redness on his inner right calf. There is a hard, tender, red cord along a visible varicose vein in the mid-calf. The calf is otherwise soft with no swelling. His temperature is 37.3°C, pulse rate 78 bpm and BP 130/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: A hard, tender, red cord along a varicose vein is superficial thrombophlebitis, a complication of varicose veins. The soft, unswollen calf argues against DVT.

steps.x: Acute painful complication of varicose veins.

clues: hard, tender, red cord along a visible varicose vein

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Diffuse spreading redness, not a cord.
Calf swelling and tenderness; the calf is soft.
Red streaks from an infected wound, with fever.
Sudden calf pain after a popliteal lump.

steps.x: **E.** Hard red cord on a varicose vein.

practice.stem: A 50 year old woman who works as a hospital porter has bulging veins in both legs. She has no previous DVT and no family history. She does not smoke. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 126/78 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely key risk factor for her varicose veins?
practice.e: Obesity is the key risk factor for varicose veins, with pregnancy and standing occupation.

steps.x: Standing job; BMI 37 in the results.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: She is a woman; female sex is the association.
She does not smoke; smoking is a PAD risk.

practice.stem: A 44 year old woman has aching legs and tortuous veins along her left medial thigh and calf. She has been referred because of pain and venous eczema. Foot pulses are present. Her pulse rate is 68 bpm and BP 118/74 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
practice.e: Duplex venous ultrasound is the gold standard: it shows reflux and valve incompetence and confirms deep vein patency.

clues: tortuous veins along her left medial thigh and calf
steps.x: Symptomatic great saphenous varicosities with skin change.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Checks arteries before compression, does not confirm reflux.

practice.stem: A 72 year old man with varicose veins is not fit for any intervention. He wants compression stockings for symptom relief. He smokes and has calf pain on walking 200 m. Foot pulses are weak. His pulse rate is 80 bpm and BP 150/88 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation before prescribing stockings?
practice.e: Compression is contraindicated if ABPI is below 0.8, so check ABPI first, especially with claudication and weak pulses.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Heart function is not the question.
Not a safety check for compression.

practice.stem: A 49 year old woman has painful varicose veins of the right leg affecting her work. Duplex ultrasound shows great saphenous reflux with patent deep veins. She has tried leg elevation and weight loss. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 126/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate treatment?
practice.e: Endothermal ablation (EVLA or radiofrequency) is the first-line interventional treatment for symptomatic great saphenous reflux.

clues: great saphenous reflux with patent deep veins
tried leg elevation and weight loss
steps.x: Confirmed reflux, deep veins fine, conservative tried.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

practice.stem: A 57 year old woman with varicose veins has a hard, tender, red cord along her great saphenous vein in the upper inner thigh. Duplex ultrasound shows superficial thrombus extending to within 2 cm of the saphenofemoral junction, with no DVT. Her temperature is 37.2°C, pulse rate 80 bpm and BP 132/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
o: NSAID and low molecular weight heparin
practice.e: Superficial thrombophlebitis is treated with NSAIDs, adding LMWH when it is extensive or near the saphenofemoral junction.

clues: within 2 cm of the saphenofemoral junction

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: Does not prevent extension into the femoral vein.

practice.stem: A 74 year old man has symptomatic varicose veins and is not fit for ablation, sclerotherapy or surgery. He also has intermittent claudication. His pulse rate is 78 bpm and BP 148/86 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
o: Leg elevation, weight loss and exercise
practice.e: Compression is contraindicated with ABPI below 0.8. He is unfit for intervention, so conservative measures are appropriate.

clues: not fit for ablation, sclerotherapy or surgery
steps.x: Conservative only; ABPI 0.62 in the results.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking

elim: He is unfit for sclerotherapy, which is ultrasound-guided.

practice.stem: A 63 year old woman with varicose veins for many years has brown staining of the skin above both medial malleoli. Her pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 130/78 mmHg. Foot pulses are present.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause of the brown staining?
practice.e: Venous hypertension damages capillaries, red cells leak out and their haemosiderin stains the skin brown.

steps.x: Chronic venous insufficiency at the gaiter area.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Haemosiderin** from red cells leaking through damaged capillaries.

elim: Melanocyte change gives moles or melasma.
